characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EMPYREAN, PANALYTICAL with Co-Kα source (operating voltage 40 kV; operating current 40 mA)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Elemental diffraction peaks of Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si, C decrease with milling time and low-intensity peaks vanish after 5 h; solid solution formed after 25 h (BCC + γ-brass type); B2-type ordered phase coexists after 35 h; trace Si remains undissolved
characterization_methods.purpose: Ascertain alloying behaviour during milling and phase formation

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GSAS-II (general structural analysis system); Chebyschev-I background with 10 coefficients; pseudo-Voigt profile; uniaxial model
characterization_methods.key_findings: 35 h weight fractions: BCC 64.0, γ-brass type 27.0, B2-type 6.0, Si 3.0; crystallite sizes: BCC 13 nm, γ-brass type 10 nm, B2-type 13 nm, Si 14 nm; BCC dislocation density 3.97 ×10^18 m^-2
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine lattice parameter, crystallite size, microstrain, phase fraction and dislocation density

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Evo 18 Carl Zeiss SEM and FEI Nova Nano SEM 450 FE-SEM, both equipped with EDS detector
characterization_methods.key_findings: Particles refine with milling; 35 h powder shows three contrasts (white, light grey, dark grey); light grey regions Fe-rich (BCC), dark grey regions Mn-rich (γ-brass type); mean particle size 3-5 µm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: powder milled 10, 20, 30 and 35 h; 2 µm scale-bar micrographs; full-area, spot 1 and spot 2 EDS
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine microstructural features, chemical analysis and elemental mapping of milled powder at different milling times
characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and field emission SEM (FE-SEM) with EDS

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TECNAI G2 T20, FEI, operating at 200 kV

analytical_models.model_note: Inputs are binary liquidus temperatures and semi-empirical Miedema binary mixing enthalpies of the constituent pairs (Table 1). ML prediction reported as more precise than rule of mixture.

computational_details.simulation_method: Machine learning (ML) approach formula and rule of mixture

analytical_models.equation_role: Predicting disordered solid solution / phase formation in HEAs
analytical_models.model_name: ΔH_mix, ΔS_conf, δ, Ω and VEC criteria for regular solid solution formation
analytical_models.model_note: Values compared to criteria for regular solid solution (−22 ≤ ΔH_mix ≤ 7; 11 ≤ ΔS_conf ≤ 19.5; δ ≤ 6.6; Ω ≥ 1.1); VEC = 6.9 lies in the 6.87 < VEC < 8.0 BCC + FCC band while δ = 7.6 % exceeds the criterion.

computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic parameter calculation for solid-solution formation (Boltzmann hypothesis, Miedema model, Zhang's approach)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: VEC within the dual-phase (BCC+FCC) range and within solid-solution formation criteria; the alloy forms BCC type structure in the milled and SPSed samples

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Pressure = 100000 Pa; System size = 1.0 mol; Mole fraction Mn = 0.19, Ni = 0.15, Al = 0.15, Si = 0.1, C = 0.01
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD modelling and single-point equilibrium calculation
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Differences between experimental and CALPHAD predicted phases attributed to using the TCFE8 database instead of TCHEA3

interfaces.phase_evolution: During milling the elemental XRD peaks diminish; solid solution forms after 25 h giving BCC (a = 0.286 nm) and γ-brass type (a = 0.872 nm). Extending milling to 35 h introduces a partially ordered B2-type phase (a = 0.290 nm) coexisting with the other phases and a decrease in the amount of Si; a trace amount of Si remains undissolved even after 35 h. The 35 h milled powder is thermally stable up to ~500 °C; on further heating an Fe5Si3-type (hP16) intermetallic forms from ~520 °C.

processing_steps.atmosphere: toluene process control reagent (to avoid oxidation)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Planetary ball mill (Model no. PM 400/2, Retsch) at 200 rpm; ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; tungsten carbide (WC) vials and WC balls; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating; 2-3 g of powder taken after every 5 h to follow phase evolution.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: crystallite size: BCC 13 nm, γ-brass type 10 nm, B2-type 13 nm, Si 14 nm (Table 2, 35 h); crystallite size ~13-17 nm for BCC and ~10-13 nm for γ-brass type over milling; TEM shows nanocrystalline grains after 35 h

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase nanocrystalline structure: BCC as the major phase plus γ-brass type and partially ordered B2-type phases, along with a trace amount of undissolved Si.

unmapped_findings: Nominal composition of the high entropy steel: Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 (at.%), corresponding to Fe-46.00, Mn-21.50, Ni-18.13, Al-8.34, Si-5.78, C-0.25 wt.%; starting elemental powders were 99.2% pure.

Lattice parameters of the 35 h milled powder phases (Rietveld refinement, Table 2): BCC a = 0.286 nm (volume 23.39 Å³), γ-brass type a = 0.872 nm (698.33 Å³), B2-type a = 0.290 nm (24.39 Å³), Si a = 0.543 nm (160.10 Å³).
For the 35 h milled powder, Rietveld fit quality: GoF = 1.10, χ² = 1.22 (Table 2).
Mean particle size of the 35 h milled powder is 3-5 µm (histogram average ~4 ± 1 µm); SEM shows three contrast levels (white, light grey, dark grey) and bulky, irregular particle shapes.

Full-area EDS composition of the 35 h milled powder: Fe 42.0, Mn 21.0, Ni 13.0, Al 13.0, Si 9.0 at.%; Spot 1: Fe 54.0, Mn 22.0, Ni 14.0, Al 6.0, Si 4.0 at.%; Spot 2 (Mn-rich): Fe 34.0, Mn 61.0, Ni 0.6, Al 4.0, Si 0.2 at.%.

Carbon dissolved fastest during milling due to its small atomic size and high diffusivity; Al dissolved next, followed by Mn and Ni; Si remained undissolved after 35 h due to the lowest self-diffusion coefficient and non-metallic behaviour.
The lattice parameter of the major BCC phase formed during milling is close to ferritic iron (α-Fe), acting as the host lattice.
No contamination (from WC vials/balls) was observed in the 35 h milled powder as discerned by X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy.
Elemental self-diffusion coefficients used to rationalise alloying (Table 7): Fe 10^-31, Mn 10^-36, Ni 10^-36, Al 10^-19, Si 10^-62 m²/s; C not reported.
Theoretical density of the alloy computed by rule of mixture is 6.55 g/cc; the SPSed pellet (not this powder sample) had ~99% relative density and 6.49 ± 0.3 g/cc experimental density.
